Parses data.noun/data.adj raw WNDB records directly: 'offset lex_filenum ss_type w_cnt {word lex_id}*w_cnt p_cnt {ptr_sym target_offset target_pos src/tgt}*p_cnt | gloss' (w_cnt hex, p_cnt decimal, per wndb(5WN)). index.noun/index.adj used only to obtain each lemma's sense-ordered synset-offset list (index files list a lemma's offsets in sense-number order; sense 1 = first offset). index.sense's explicit sense_number field was used to cross-check the light/dark adjective sense-number claims (see illumination.adjective_route.exclusion_demonstration). data.verb/data.adv/index.verb/index.adv are checksummed for citability but not used: the task specifies noun+adjective routes only.

noun_route.rule: Root selection: for lemma L, L.n.NN = the NN-th offset in index.noun's space-separated offset list for L (sense-number order). chromatic_color.n.01 = sense 1 of 'chromatic_color' (index.noun lists exactly 1 sense) = offset 04959672; color.n.01 = sense 1 of 'color' (of 8 senses) = offset 04956594. Both cross-checked against gloss text. CLOSURE(root) = the set of synset offsets reachable from root by transitively following every '~' (Hyponym) / '~i' (Instance Hyponym) pointer recorded on the current synset in data.noun, restricted to pointer target pos='n' (WordNet stores the hyponym pointer explicitly on the parent synset itself, so no inversion of hypernym pointers is needed). Root's own lemmas are excluded from closure entries (a synset is not its own hyponym); each non-root synset in the closure contributes one entry per lemma it carries. chromatic_color.n.01 and color.n.01 closures are reported SEPARATELY per instruction, not merged. 'color.n.01's direct hyponym tree' is read as the SAME full transitive-closure mechanism (WordNet's own browser interface labels the '~' relation itself 'direct hyponym', expandable to the full tree) so the two routes are mechanically identical in kind; color.n.01's immediate 1-hop hyponyms (9 synsets) are ALSO reported separately as a supplementary table in case a shallow (1-hop-only) reading of 'direct' was intended -- this ambiguity is flagged, not silently resolved. achromatic_color.n.01's closure (15 synsets) is reported as a second supplementary table because color.n.01's closure decomposes exactly into chromatic_color.n.01's ∪ achromatic_color.n.01's ∪ a 30-synset remainder (skin/hair-pigmentation and color-quality-abstraction vocabulary under neither pole) -- verified: both sub-closures ⊆ color.n.01's closure, and disjoint from each other (0 overlap).

adjective_route.rule: Adjective 'cluster' = a HEAD synset (ss_type='a') plus every SATELLITE synset (ss_type='s') it points to via a '&' (Similar-to) pointer. Verified globally over all of data.adj: every satellite carries EXACTLY ONE '&' pointer, always to a head (10693/10693 satellites checked; 0 head-to-head '&' edges) -- a clean two-level structure, so CLUSTER(head)={head} ∪ {s : s --&--> head} is complete with no recursion needed. Head selection (mechanical, not gloss-eyeballed): 'colored' -- among its 4 index.adj senses, the unique ss_type='a' one (offset 00394562; the other 3 are satellites of unrelated heads -- racial/skin-color 00242575, biased 01723091, dyed/bleached 01572171 -- excluded automatically by the ss_type filter). 'chromatic' -- among its 3 index.adj senses (all ss_type='a'), the one carrying an attribute (=) pointer to hue.n.01 (offset 04975122); the other two (an optics/lens sense 02956623, a music/'chromatic scale' sense 00409750) are excluded automatically by the attribute-pointer filter. CRITERION (i) = membership in CLUSTER(00394562) ∪ CLUSTER(00366691). CRITERION (ii) = the synset's definition text (gloss up to the first ';', WordNet's own definition/example delimiter) matches the case-insensitive regex ^of (the|a) colou?r\b -- i.e. literally begins 'of the color/colour' or 'of a color/colour' (covers 'of the color of X' and 'of a color similar to/resembling/intermediate between X', the shapes actually attested in this file). Applied to ALL of data.adj, independent of cluster membership -- the task states no cluster-membership restriction for this arm. Full color-adjective route = CRITERION (i) ∪ CRITERION (ii); every entry's route field records exactly which criterion/criteria fired and which head cluster (if any) it belongs to.

structural_note_achromatic_a01_NOT_in_of.explanation: achromatic.a.01 {achromatic, neutral} 'having no hue' is the antonym/sibling of chromatic.a.03 (shares the same hue.n.01 attribute target) and heads a 46-satellite cluster of genuine achromatic color adjectives (grey, silvery, ash-grey, jet-black, milk-white, ...). The task names only 'colored'/'chromatic' as cluster heads, so this cluster is NOT part of the official color-adjective route; only 2 of its 46 satellites (ink-black, slate-grey) enter via the gloss-pattern criterion. This produces a noun/adjective-route asymmetry: achromatic color WORDS are in the noun route (color.n.01 ⊇ achromatic_color.n.01's 15-synset closure) but achromatic color ADJECTIVES are almost entirely absent from the adjective route. Reported as found; not amended.
